title: Site use - hours (OBP method)
section: Site use adjusted for detection gap threshold
text:
Site use adjusted for detection gap threshold

Detection threshold
To define independent observations, we needed a time gap that separates a bird leaving a site from just briefly dropping out of antenna range (e.g., by turning away or moving behind vegetation). Short gaps likely mean the bird is still present; long gaps likely mean it has left. We analysed the distribution of time gaps between successive detection runs of the same bird at the same station, and across all individuals, and used this to choose a cut-off separating “same visit” from “new visit”. A three-component mixture model (MIXTOOLS 2.0.0.1) was fitted to the gap durations, distinguishing short gaps (same visit) from medium/long gaps (new visit). Gaps were truncated to 5 min – 30 hours to remove noise from very short or very long outliers, and each gap was classified by whichever distribution best matched it.
1. Build run-level summary (one row per run) from hits. A “run” is already identified by runID in data_all (see Motus documentation - Chapter 3). We need the start/end time of each run, per individual and per station.

runs <- data_all %>%
  group_by(speciesEN, Band.ID, recvDeployName, runID) %>%
  summarise(
    runStart = min(timeAus, na.rm = TRUE),
    runEnd   = max(timeAus, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_detect = n(), 
    .groups = "drop")

2. Compute gaps between successive runs of the same individual at the same antenna/site.

gaps <- runs %>%
  arrange(Band.ID, recvDeployName, runStart) %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, recvDeployName) %>%
  mutate(
    prevRunEnd = lag(runEnd),
    gapHours   = round(as.numeric(difftime(runStart, prevRunEnd, units = "hours")), 2)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(gapHours)) %>%
  filter(gapHours > 0) # we are not dealing with overlaps yet (simultaneous detection of the same tag from two or more antenna)

3. Truncate gaps (hours) for mixture model fitting. ::: blockquote-yellow NOTE: Below are values you should choose based on your own data and on the ecological plausibility of your system. :::























4. Fit a 3-component normal mixture model. Now we have visually explored how data is distributed to select a gap threshold value, we might use statistical model to assess this value more systematical and based on the data only, besides visual selection accounting for ecologically plausibility.

gap_trunc <- gaps %>%
  filter(gapHours > 0.3,     # ~5 minutes                   
         gapHours < 30) %>%  # 30 hours
  pull(gapHours)

set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility of EM starting values

mix_model <- normalmixEM(
  gap_trunc,
  k = 3,
  maxit = 5000,
  epsilon = 1e-08)

number of iterations= 150 

summary(mix_model)

summary of normalmixEM object:
         comp 1   comp 2     comp 3
lambda 0.324799 0.587364  0.0878374
mu     0.696852 9.275983 23.9154082
sigma  0.352310 6.131985  0.4628914
loglik at estimate:  -12830.01 


6. Find the threshold value, the cut-point: the gap value where classification switches from “Non-independent” to an “Independent” class (i.e. where posterior prob of the non-independent component drops below 0.5 as gap duration increases). We will first classify each gap to the component with highest posterior probability, and order components by their mean, so component 1 = shortest-gap (non-independent), 2 = medium, 3 = long (independent).











Define used time (hours)
Now, we decide to merge into one and unique continuous detection, all the tags (birds) detected per a same antenna, including gaps under a duration of 1 (one) hour. Although the model is highlighting a value of 1.57, we decided to remain conservative.
Once detection data summarised as described above, we can see, overall, how long birds stay around one Motus station - see plot below.









*Note Newcastle NSW tides are turning ~6h cycles between high/low, and our birds seem to mostly visits any site less than 3 hours. An early descriptive sign of site use very tide dependent, as they would stay about 3 hours in the same area, around the highest/lowest point of the tide line, before to leave site, as the tide might be rising or receiving.*









To avoid inflating site use duration estimates with the very few individuals showing more than 25 hours of continuous presence in the same area, we excluded these cases. Such extended duration likely reflect a dropped tag rather than genuine site fidelity. Verifying each case individually would be time-consuming, so we treat this as a working assumption for now; should this pattern become more frequent in future data, it would warrant closer investigation.

visit_duration <- visit_duration %>%
         filter(duration_h < 25)

It remains to attribute at each visit period a tide category. We expand each visit into hourly bins spanning visitStart to visitEnd (visit_duration itself is untouched). Then, we compute exact overlap (in hours) between each hourly bin and the actual visit window.

visit_hours <- visit_duration %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(hour_dt = list(seq(from = floor_date(visitStart, "hour"),
                             to   = floor_date(visitEnd, "hour"),
                             by   = "hour"))) %>%
  unnest(cols = c(hour_dt)) %>%
  ungroup()

visit_hours <- visit_hours %>%
  mutate(
    bin_start     = hour_dt,
    bin_end       = hour_dt + hours(1),
    overlap_start = pmax(visitStart, bin_start),
    overlap_end   = pmin(visitEnd, bin_end),
    overlap_h     = as.numeric(difftime(overlap_end, overlap_start, units = "hours"))
  ) %>%
  filter(overlap_h > 0)   # drops bins with no actual overlap

# Attach nearest tide category to each hourly bin
tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[, .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]
setkey(tide_dt, tideDateTimeAus)

vh_dt <- as.data.table(visit_hours)
setkey(vh_dt, hour_dt)

visit_hours_tide <- tide_dt[vh_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
setnames(visit_hours_tide, "tideDateTimeAus", "hour_dt")

Let’s finalise the table giving data for detection relative to the trio bird-station-tide.

used_bird_recv_time <- visit_hours_tide %>%
  mutate(tideDiel = if_else(grepl("Diurnal", tideCategory), "Diurnal", "Nocturnal"),
         tideHighLow = if_else(grepl("High", tideCategory), "High", "Low")) %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, recvDeployName, tideCategory, tideDiel, tideHighLow) %>%
  summarise(duration_h = sum(overlap_h), .groups = "drop")



Define available time (hours)
Now used time addressed, we need to define for each individual (birds) and across each Motus stations, what was the amount of time available for the four tide categories.
Available time for each Motus stations is accessed with activity table: each row is a dated record of noise or a tag detected - see Survey effort > Activity table.
We need to extract the temporal coverage of each station, starting from deployment date to the last recorded activity (noise or detection).
# Sort the terminated serno (if terminated, ie. one box removed from one antenna site, a date comes along)
# but still needed for accessing survey effort as the station is currently running with another serno 
recv.act.term <- recv.act %>%
  left_join(recv %>% 
              filter(!is.na(timeEndAus)) %>%
              select(deviceID, serno, recvDeployName),
            "deviceID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(recvDeployName)) %>%
  mutate(SernoStation = paste0(recvDeployName, "_", serno))

# Sort the currently running serno
recv.act.runn <- recv.act %>%
  left_join(recv %>% 
              filter(is.na(timeEndAus)) %>%
              select(deviceID, serno, recvDeployName),
            "deviceID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(recvDeployName)) %>%
  mutate(SernoStation = paste0(recvDeployName, "_", serno))

# Merging in one data-set to use Station's name further + pick-up the rounded hours
recv.act <- bind_rows(recv.act.runn, recv.act.term) %>%
  mutate(hour_dt = round_date(dateAus, "hour"))

# Providing helpful variables
recv <- recv %>%
  mutate(SernoStation = paste0(recvDeployName, "_", serno),
         lisStart = timeStartAus,
         lisEnd = if_else(
           is.na(timeEndAus), # means the station is still running since the last data downloading
           with_tz(Sys.time(), "Australia/Sydney"),
           with_tz(as_datetime(timeEndAus, tz = "UTC"), "Australia/Sydney")) )

# Generating hourly sequences per SernoStation from start to end dates of the deviceID at particular sites
recv_hours <- recv %>%
  select(recvDeployName, deviceID, SernoStation, lisStart, lisEnd) %>%
  group_by(SernoStation) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(hour_dt = list(seq(from = round_date(lisStart, unit = "hour"),
                            to = round_date(lisEnd, unit = "hour"),
                            by = "hour")) ) %>%
  unnest(cols = c(hour_dt)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Simplify station variables (recvDeployName)
recv <- recv %>% 
  select(!recvDeployName) 
recv$recvDeployName <- sub("_SG-.*", "", recv$SernoStation)

recv_hours <- recv_hours %>% 
  select(!recvDeployName) 
recv_hours$recvDeployName <- sub("_SG-.*", "", recv_hours$SernoStation)

We now how the complete temporal coverage, expanded in hours and for each Motus station so it matches with our used time dataset.
However, due to some temporary failures or maintenance (see Survey effort > Operational periods), the actual period a station was operational may be different than the complete temporal coverage. So, we must determine when a station was not operational and substrate these off-hours to the complete temporal coverage.

# Distinguish station from mixed recv + Giving operational variable (= TRUE when existing values from act table)
recv_hours <- recv_hours %>%
  select(-any_of("operational")) %>%   # drop if it already exists, no-op if it doesn't
  left_join(recv.act %>%
              distinct(recvDeployName, hour_dt) %>%
              mutate(operational = TRUE),
            by = c("recvDeployName", "hour_dt")) %>%
  mutate(operational = if_else(is.na(operational), FALSE, TRUE))

# /!\ Due to unknown error? Have to set this manually
recv_hours <- recv_hours %>%
  mutate(operational = case_when(
    recvDeployName == "Fullerton Entrance" & 
      hour_dt > as.POSIXct("2023-04-02") & 
      hour_dt < as.POSIXct("2023-04-05") ~ FALSE,
    TRUE ~ operational))

# Only the hours the station was actually ON — computed once, no regeneration of gaps
valid_station_hours <- recv_hours %>%
  filter(operational == TRUE) %>%
  distinct(recvDeployName, hour_dt)

# Attach nearest tide category directly (this also folds in the Point 7 fix —
tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[, .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]
setkey(tide_dt, tideDateTimeAus)

vsh_dt <- as.data.table(valid_station_hours)
setkey(vsh_dt, hour_dt)

valid_station_hours_tide <- tide_dt[vsh_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
setnames(valid_station_hours_tide, "tideDateTimeAus", "hour_dt")

Temporal coverage for each station is now reduced to its operational periods. We now assign each bird its own available time period, spanning from its tagging date to its last Motus detection, and expanded to hourly resolution too.

# Get the monitored period of each bird
period_sp <- data_all  %>%
  group_by(Band.ID) %>%
  reframe(DateAUS.Trap = first(DateAUS.Trap), 
          last_dateAus = max(timeAus),
          speciesEN = first(speciesEN)) %>%
  unique()

# Expand one row per hours to each individual across its whole period (this is the available time)
bird_hours <- period_sp %>%
  group_by(Band.ID) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(hour_dt = list(seq(from = as.POSIXct(ymd(DateAUS.Trap), tz = "UTC"),
                            to = as.POSIXct(last_dateAus, tz = "UTC"),
                            by = "hour"))) %>%
  unnest(cols = c(hour_dt)) %>%
  ungroup() 

# Duplicate in as many list as many stations
recv_names <- unique(valid_station_hours_tide$recvDeployName)
bird_data_list <- setNames(vector("list", length(recv_names)), recv_names)

for(name in recv_names) {
  valid_hours_recv <- valid_station_hours_tide %>%
    filter(recvDeployName == name) %>%
    pull(hour_dt)
  
  valid_hours_bird_recv <- bird_hours %>%
    filter(hour_dt %in% valid_hours_recv)
  
  valid_hours_bird_recv$name <- name
  bird_data_list[[name]] <- valid_hours_bird_recv
}

# # FINALISE AVAILABLE TIME 
available_bird_recv_time <- bind_rows(bird_data_list) %>%
  mutate(hour_dt = force_tz(hour_dt, "Australia/Sydney")) %>%
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.))) %>%
  rename(recvDeployName = name) %>%
  left_join(valid_station_hours_tide, by = c("recvDeployName", "hour_dt")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(tideCategory)) %>%    # bird-hours the station wasn't actually ON for get dropped here
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, recvDeployName, tideCategory) %>%
  summarise(duration_h = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(tideDiel = if_else(grepl("Diurnal", tideCategory), "Diurnal", "Nocturnal"),
         tideHighLow = if_else(grepl("High", tideCategory), "High", "Low")) %>%
  select(Band.ID, speciesEN, recvDeployName, tideCategory, tideDiel, tideHighLow, duration_h)

The available time is now defined for each bird across each Motus station, taking into account the periods where stations where ON only. In the data, the available periods are expanded in hours and the tide condition is associated. While most of the couple station listening-bird tagged are potentially detectable between 0 and 1000 hours; note two small peaks around 2700 and 4000 hours of detectability potential as it might be relative to the oldest couple ON.


























Define rate of Use (%)
Now that the used and available time have been determined for each individual and for each Motus station, we can relate these two elements together with the Usage rate (or rate of use).

\[
\text{Usage rate} = \frac{\text{Time used}}{\text{Time available}} \times 100 \quad \textit{across stations and species}
\]


use_rate_plot <- used_bird_recv_time %>%
  select(-tideDiel, -tideHighLow) %>%   # drop here, keep the copy from available_bird_recv_time
  rename(used_h = duration_h) %>%
  
  left_join(available_bird_recv_time %>%
      rename(available_h = duration_h),   
    by = c("Band.ID", "speciesEN", "recvDeployName", "tideCategory")) %>%
  
  mutate(rate_use = (used_h / available_h) * 100) %>%
  select(Band.ID, speciesEN, recvDeployName, tideCategory, 
         tideDiel, tideHighLow, used_h, available_h, rate_use)


Note: A very few cases (n = 2) where the time used was over the time available has been excluded from the data. Reasons might be the tag fell off within range of the antenna. Due to the negligible number of such cases, we have not further investigated.














Nocturna




use_rate_plot <- use_rate_plot %>%
  filter(rate_use < 100)


Note: We filtered out Masked Lapwing from the analysis, since they have too few data.

  mutate(speciesType = factor(shorebird_class[speciesEN], 
                               levels = c("migratory", "resident"))) %>%
  
  filter(!speciesEN %in% c("Masked Lapwing"))

title: Fullerton Entrance (Fly-by vs Site Use)
text:
Why this station is treated differently
Fullerton Entrance carries a single directional Yagi antenna (6-elements). Unlike the small omni-directional antennas used across the rest of the Motus array in the Hunter estuary (see Motus Array Maintenance), and capable of tracking site use directly, Fullerton Entrance station is located strategically: it sits on the corridor between the main area (estuary covered by several omni antennas) and the biggest and main mudflat of the area (Fullerton Cove), which has no antenna coverage at all because of its terrain configuration. So, in order to track movement and site use over this big mudflat (Fullerton Cove, or also called Fullerton mudflat), we placed a station right at the entry (Fullerton Entrance), to detect in-and-out passages.
Therefore, a tag detection at Fullerton Entrance station is either:

fly-by, the bird briefly fly by (in front of) the antenna, probably traveling between the estuary (roost?) and Fullerton mudflat (foraging?)
site use - the bird is actually sitting by the antenna itself, either roosting or foraging, using the site.

Since we cannot detect birds directly on Fullerton mudflat, we use fly-by detections at Fullerton Entrance station and their direction (another station → Fullerton Entrance or another station → Fullerton Entrance) as an indirect proxy for mudflat use.

title: Fullerton Entrance - Flyby vs Site Use
section: Step 1 - Separate flybys from actual site use
text:
Step 1 - Separate flybys from actual site use
Not every detection at Fullerton Entrance represents the same behaviour. A very short visit (seconds to a couple of minutes) most likely reflects a bird flying past the antenna’s beam; a longer visit likely reflects a bird actually stopping in range of the antenna. We use the same mixture-model approach as for the detection-gap threshold (see previous chapter), but here fitted to visit durations at Fullerton Entrance only, to find a data-driven cut-off between “flyby” and “actual use”.

focal_station    <- "Fullerton Entrance"   # the directional antenna
flyby_window_min <- 30                     # minutes before/after a Fullerton detection to look
                                            # for a detection at another station
tide_lookahead_h <- 2                      # hours ahead of an "unknown" flyby used to infer
                                            # direction from tide state

stopifnot(focal_station %in% unique(visit_duration$recvDeployName))

fc_visits <- visit_duration %>%
  filter(recvDeployName == focal_station) %>%
  mutate(duration_min = duration_h * 60)

Fit a 2-component mixture model on log-transformed visit duration (component 1 = short/flyby, component 2 = long/actual use), and find the cut-point where the posterior probability of belonging to the “flyby” component drops below 0.5.

set.seed(123)
mix_fc <- normalmixEM(
  log(fc_visits$duration_min + 1),   # +1 to avoid log(0)
  k = 2,
  maxit = 5000,
  epsilon = 1e-08)

number of iterations= 21 

comp_order_fc <- order(mix_fc$mu)
post_short    <- mix_fc$posterior[, comp_order_fc[1]]

cut_df <- data.frame(duration_h = fc_visits$duration_h,
                     p_short = post_short) %>%
  arrange(duration_h)

flyby_cutpoint_h <- cut_df$duration_h[which(cut_df$p_short < 0.5)[1]]
cat("Flyby / actual-use cutpoint at", focal_station, ":",
    round(flyby_cutpoint_h, 2), "hours (~", round(flyby_cutpoint_h * 60, 1), "min)\n")

Flyby / actual-use cutpoint at Fullerton Entrance : 0.18 hours (~ 10.8 min)



fc_visits <- fc_visits %>%
  mutate(visit_type = if_else(duration_h < flyby_cutpoint_h, "flyby", "actual_use"))

title: Fullerton Entrance - Flyby vs Site Use
section: Step 2 - Infer the direction of each flyby
text:
Step 2 - Infer the direction of each flyby
For flyby events specifically, we want to know whether the bird was heading to the mudflat (last seen leaving the roost area, i.e. detected at another station shortly before the flyby) or coming from the mudflat (detected at another station shortly after the flyby). If both are true, the bird is treated as a return_flight seen at Fullerton Entrance on the way out and back; if neither, the direction is unknown and resolved separately using tide state (see below).

flyby_visits <- fc_visits %>% filter(visit_type == "flyby")

all_visits_dt   <- as.data.table(visit_duration)
other_visits_dt <- all_visits_dt[recvDeployName != focal_station]
flyby_dt        <- as.data.table(flyby_visits)

BEFORE match - closest other-station visit that ended within flyby_window_min minutes before the flyby started.

before_cand <- other_visits_dt[flyby_dt,
                               on = "Band.ID",
                               allow.cartesian = TRUE,
                               .(Band.ID, visitID = i.visitID,
                                 fc_start = i.visitStart,
                                 other_station = x.recvDeployName,
                                 other_end = x.visitEnd)]

before_cand <- before_cand[!is.na(other_end) &
                             other_end <= fc_start &
                             as.numeric(difftime(fc_start, other_end, units = "mins")) <= flyby_window_min]

# Keep only the closest (most recent) match per flyby event
before_flag <- before_cand[order(Band.ID, visitID, -as.numeric(other_end))][
  , .SD[1], by = .(Band.ID, visitID)][
  , .(Band.ID, visitID, before_station = other_station, before_end = other_end)]

AFTER match - closest other-station visit that started within flyby_window_min minutes after the flyby ended (mirror image of the BEFORE match above).

after_cand <- other_visits_dt[flyby_dt,
                              on = "Band.ID",
                              allow.cartesian = TRUE,
                              .(Band.ID, visitID = i.visitID,
                                fc_end = i.visitEnd,
                                other_station = x.recvDeployName,
                                other_start = x.visitStart)]

after_cand <- after_cand[!is.na(other_start) &
                           other_start >= fc_end &
                           as.numeric(difftime(other_start, fc_end, units = "mins")) <= flyby_window_min]

# Keep only the closest (earliest) match per flyby event
after_flag <- after_cand[order(Band.ID, visitID, as.numeric(other_start))][
  , .SD[1], by = .(Band.ID, visitID)][
  , .(Band.ID, visitID, after_station = other_station, after_start = other_start)]

Classify direction from the presence/absence of a BEFORE and/or AFTER match.

flyby_direction <- flyby_visits %>%
  left_join(as.data.frame(before_flag), by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  left_join(as.data.frame(after_flag),  by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(
    has_before = !is.na(before_end),
    has_after  = !is.na(after_start),
    direction = case_when(
      has_before & has_after  ~ "return_flight",
      has_before & !has_after ~ "to_mudflat",
      !has_before & has_after ~ "from_mudflat",
      TRUE                    ~ "unknown"))


Resolving the “unknown” flybys with tide state
For flybys with no other-station match on either side, direction cannot be resolved from detections alone. As a fallback, we look at the tide state around the flyby: if the tide is rising toward High in the following hours, the bird is more likely heading from the mudflat (leaving as it floods); if it is falling toward Low, the bird is more likely heading to the mudflat (arriving as it drains).

tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[, .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]
setkey(tide_dt, tideDateTimeAus)

infer_tide_direction <- function(start_time, lookahead_h = tide_lookahead_h) {
  hrs    <- seq(from = start_time, by = "hour", length.out = lookahead_h + 1)
  hrs_dt <- data.table(hour_dt = hrs)
  matched <- tide_dt[hrs_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
  n_high <- sum(grepl("High", matched$tideCategory))
  n_low  <- sum(grepl("Low",  matched$tideCategory))
  if (n_high > n_low) return("from_mudflat_tide")
  if (n_low > n_high) return("to_mudflat_tide")
  "ambiguous_tide"
}

unknown_flyby <- flyby_direction %>%
  filter(direction == "unknown") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(inferred_direction = infer_tide_direction(visitStart)) %>%
  ungroup()

flyby_direction <- flyby_direction %>%
  left_join(unknown_flyby %>% select(Band.ID, visitID, inferred_direction),
            by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(direction_final = if_else(direction == "unknown" & !is.na(inferred_direction),
                                    inferred_direction, direction))










We simplify direction_final into a broader direction_class (from / to / return / other) for plotting.

flyby_direction <- flyby_direction %>%
  mutate(
    direction_class = case_when(
      direction_final %in% c("from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide") ~ "from",
      direction_final %in% c("to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide")     ~ "to",
      direction_final == "return_flight"                          ~ "return",
      TRUE                                                        ~ "other"),
    direction_class = factor(direction_class, levels = c("from", "to", "return", "other")))

title: Fullerton Entrance (Fly-by vs Site Use)
section: Step 3 - Combine flyby and site-use classifications
text:
Step 3 - Combine flyby and site-use classifications
We now bring visit_type (flyby / actual_use) and direction_final back together into a single table covering all Fullerton Entrance visits, so that “site use” sits alongside the flyby directions as one classification.

fc_classified <- fc_visits %>%
  left_join(
    flyby_direction %>%
      select(Band.ID, visitID, direction, direction_final),
    by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(direction_final = if_else(visit_type == "actual_use", "site_use", direction_final))

title: Fullerton Entrance (Fly-by vs Site Use)
section: Step 4 - Estimate hours spent at the mudflat vs at Fullerton Entrance
text:
Step 4 - Estimate hours spent at the mudflat vs at Fullerton Entrance
For site_use events, the duration a bird spent at Fullerton Entrance is simply duration_h of the visit itself. For to_mudflat/from_mudflat flybys there is no direct duration - instead we use the surrounding tide turning point as a proxy boundary for how long the bird likely remained on the mudflat:

to_mudflat - from the moment the bird was last seen (visitEnd) forward to the next tide turning point (i.e. the remainder of the current tide phase).
from_mudflat - from the previous tide turning point back to the moment the bird was detected (visitStart) (i.e. how long the current tide phase had already run before the bird arrived).


# Nearest tide turning point before / after a given timestamp
tide_times <- sort(tide_data$tideDateTimeAus)

next_tide_turn <- function(t) {
  cand <- tide_times[tide_times > t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  min(cand)
}
prev_tide_turn <- function(t) {
  cand <- tide_times[tide_times < t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  max(cand)
}

# Dominant tideCategory across a time window (hourly expansion, nearest-tide join)
tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[order(tideDateTimeAus), .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]

dominant_tide <- function(w_start, w_end) {
  if (is.na(w_start) || is.na(w_end) || w_end <= w_start) return(NA_character_)
  hrs    <- seq(floor_date(w_start, "hour"), floor_date(w_end, "hour"), by = "hour")
  hrs_dt <- data.table(hour_dt = hrs)
  matched <- tide_dt[hrs_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
  names(sort(table(matched$tideCategory), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
}

Build the per-visit duration/tide table, keeping only site_use and mudflat-direction events (return flights and unresolved flybys are excluded, since we cannot bound a mudflat window for them).

plot_data <- fc_classified %>%
  filter(direction_final %in% c("site_use", "to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide",
                                "from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    category = if_else(direction_final == "site_use",
                       "Fullerton entrance", "Fullerton mudflat"),
    win_start = case_when(
      direction_final == "site_use" ~ visitStart,
      direction_final %in% c("to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide")   ~ visitEnd,
      direction_final %in% c("from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide") ~ prev_tide_turn(visitStart)),
    win_end = case_when(
      direction_final == "site_use" ~ visitEnd,
      direction_final %in% c("to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide")   ~ next_tide_turn(visitEnd),
      direction_final %in% c("from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide") ~ visitStart),
    duration_h_final = as.numeric(difftime(win_end, win_start, units = "hours")),
    tideCategory_dom  = dominant_tide(win_start, win_end),
    tideDiel = if_else(grepl("Diurnal", tideCategory_dom), "Diurnal", "Nocturnal")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(duration_h_final), duration_h_final > 0)


Rate of use, referenced to Fullerton Entrance availability
Because “Fullerton mudflat” is an inferred location rather than a real receiver, both categories are expressed as a rate against the same denominator: the hours Fullerton Entrance was available (station on + bird tagged and alive), per bird and per diel period. This comes from available_bird_recv_time, computed in the previous chapter.

# Available hours at Fullerton Entrance, per bird / species / diel period
available_fc <- available_bird_recv_time %>%
  filter(recvDeployName == "Fullerton Entrance") %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, tideDiel) %>%
  summarise(available_h = sum(duration_h), .groups = "drop")

# Used hours per bird / category / diel period, then compute rate of use (%)
plot_summary <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, category, tideDiel) %>%
  summarise(used_h = sum(duration_h_final), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(available_fc, by = c("Band.ID", "speciesEN", "tideDiel")) %>%
  mutate(rate_use = (used_h / available_h) * 100,
         rate_use = pmin(rate_use, 100))  # cap: a few cases exceed 100% (see note below)


Note: a small number of birds show rate_use above 100%, since mudflat duration is inferred from tide turning points rather than directly observed, and can occasionally exceed the bird’s directly-available Fullerton Entrance time. These values are capped at 100% rather than excluded.

title: Fullerton Entrance (Fly-by vs Site Use)
text:
Set-up
As we will be re-using some of the data already loaded from previous workflow (see Station usage - hours (OBP method)), we will fetch here some of the objects we will re-use including: visit_duration, tide_data, data_all, recv, shorebird_class, and available_bird_recv_time.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(mixtools)
library(lubridate)
library(gt)

Now, we pre-fill some key-values we need to set-up the workflow.

focal_station    <- "Fullerton Entrance"   # the directional antenna

flyby_window_min <- 30                     # Period (min) before/after detection at Fullerton to look for a detection at another station

tide_lookahead_h <- 2                      # Period (hours) before/after of an "unknown" flyby detection used to infer direction from tide

# Keep only Fullerton Entrance data with visit duration (min)
fc_visits <- visit_duration %>%
  filter(recvDeployName == focal_station) %>%
  mutate(duration_min = duration_h * 60)

title: Fullerton Entrance (Fly-by vs Site Use)
text:
Separate fly-by & site use
A very short visit (seconds to a couple of minutes) most likely reflects a bird flying by the antenna; while a longer visit likely reflects a bird actually using the site covered by antenna’s range coverage. We use the same mixture-model approach as for the detection-gap threshold (see Station usage - hours (OBP method)), but here fitted to visit durations at Fullerton Entrance only, to find a data-driven cut-off between “flyby” and “actual use”.
Fit a 2-component mixture model on log-transformed visit duration (component 1 = short/flyby, component 2 = long/actual use), and find the cut-point where the posterior probability of belonging to the “flyby” component drops below 0.5.

set.seed(123)

mix_fc <- normalmixEM(               # we assume normal distributions only
  log(fc_visits$duration_min + 1),   # +1 to avoid log(0), and log() used to compress/scale duration distributions and tails (i.e., lot of short vs few long)
  k = 2,                             # we assume two potential distribution (flyby and site use)
  maxit = 5000,                      # number of iteration to estimate what component each observation belogs to
  epsilon = 1e-08)                   # standard threshold value for estimation (convergence tolerance)

number of iterations= 21 

comp_order_fc <- order(mix_fc$mu)    # sort components -> comp_1 with smaller mean first (fly-by)

post_short    <- mix_fc$posterior[, comp_order_fc[1]] # extract first col of mix_fc$posterior, a matrix with one row per visit and one column per component, containing each visit's posterior probability of belonging to that component (rows sum to 1). So, post_short is a vector giving one value per visit of "probability this visit is a fly-by."

cut_df <- data.frame(duration_h = fc_visits$duration_h, p_short = post_short) %>%
  arrange(duration_h)

flyby_cutpoint_h <- cut_df$duration_h[which(cut_df$p_short < 0.5)[1]] # /!\ the value chosen here (0.5) finds the first duration in hour (smallest) where it has less than 50 % probability to be a fly-by /!\

Under 0.18 hours (~ 11 min), a detection at Fullerton Entrance is considered as a fly-by and above as a site use. So, let’s classify and visualise.

fc_visits <- fc_visits %>%
  mutate(visit_type = if_else(duration_h < flyby_cutpoint_h, "flyby", "actual_use"))

title: Fullerton Entrance (Fly-by vs Site Use)
section: Infer the direction of each flyby
text:
Infer the direction of each flyby
For flyby events specifically, we want to know whether the bird was heading to the mudflat (last seen leaving the roost area, i.e. detected at another station shortly before the flyby) or coming from the mudflat (detected at another station shortly after the flyby). If both are true, the bird is treated as a return_flight seen at Fullerton Entrance on the way out and back; if neither, the direction is unknown and resolved separately using tide state (see below).

flyby_visits <- fc_visits %>% filter(visit_type == "flyby")

all_visits_dt   <- as.data.table(visit_duration)
other_visits_dt <- all_visits_dt[recvDeployName != focal_station]
flyby_dt        <- as.data.table(flyby_visits)

BEFORE match - closest other-station visit that ended within flyby_window_min minutes before the flyby started.

before_cand <- other_visits_dt[flyby_dt,
                               on = "Band.ID",
                               allow.cartesian = TRUE,
                               .(Band.ID, visitID = i.visitID,
                                 fc_start = i.visitStart,
                                 other_station = x.recvDeployName,
                                 other_end = x.visitEnd)]

before_cand <- before_cand[!is.na(other_end) &
                             other_end <= fc_start &
                             as.numeric(difftime(fc_start, other_end, units = "mins")) <= flyby_window_min]

# Keep only the closest (most recent) match per flyby event
before_flag <- before_cand[order(Band.ID, visitID, -as.numeric(other_end))][
  , .SD[1], by = .(Band.ID, visitID)][
  , .(Band.ID, visitID, before_station = other_station, before_end = other_end)]

AFTER match - closest other-station visit that started within flyby_window_min minutes after the flyby ended (mirror image of the BEFORE match above).

after_cand <- other_visits_dt[flyby_dt,
                              on = "Band.ID",
                              allow.cartesian = TRUE,
                              .(Band.ID, visitID = i.visitID,
                                fc_end = i.visitEnd,
                                other_station = x.recvDeployName,
                                other_start = x.visitStart)]

after_cand <- after_cand[!is.na(other_start) &
                           other_start >= fc_end &
                           as.numeric(difftime(other_start, fc_end, units = "mins")) <= flyby_window_min]

# Keep only the closest (earliest) match per flyby event
after_flag <- after_cand[order(Band.ID, visitID, as.numeric(other_start))][
  , .SD[1], by = .(Band.ID, visitID)][
  , .(Band.ID, visitID, after_station = other_station, after_start = other_start)]

Classify direction from the presence/absence of a BEFORE and/or AFTER match.

flyby_direction <- flyby_visits %>%
  left_join(as.data.frame(before_flag), by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  left_join(as.data.frame(after_flag),  by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(
    has_before = !is.na(before_end),
    has_after  = !is.na(after_start),
    direction = case_when(
      has_before & has_after  ~ "return_flight",
      has_before & !has_after ~ "to_mudflat",
      !has_before & has_after ~ "from_mudflat",
      TRUE                    ~ "unknown"))


Resolving the “unknown” flybys with tide state
For flybys with no other-station match on either side, direction cannot be resolved from detections alone. As a fallback, we look at the tide state around the flyby: if the tide is rising toward High in the following hours, the bird is more likely heading from the mudflat (leaving as it floods); if it is falling toward Low, the bird is more likely heading to the mudflat (arriving as it drains).

tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[, .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]
setkey(tide_dt, tideDateTimeAus)

infer_tide_direction <- function(start_time, lookahead_h = tide_lookahead_h) {
  hrs    <- seq(from = start_time, by = "hour", length.out = lookahead_h + 1)
  hrs_dt <- data.table(hour_dt = hrs)
  matched <- tide_dt[hrs_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
  n_high <- sum(grepl("High", matched$tideCategory))
  n_low  <- sum(grepl("Low",  matched$tideCategory))
  if (n_high > n_low) return("from_mudflat_tide")
  if (n_low > n_high) return("to_mudflat_tide")
  "ambiguous_tide"
}

unknown_flyby <- flyby_direction %>%
  filter(direction == "unknown") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(inferred_direction = infer_tide_direction(visitStart)) %>%
  ungroup()

flyby_direction <- flyby_direction %>%
  left_join(unknown_flyby %>% select(Band.ID, visitID, inferred_direction),
            by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(direction_final = if_else(direction == "unknown" & !is.na(inferred_direction),
                                    inferred_direction, direction))










We simplify direction_final into a broader direction_class (from / to / return / other) for plotting.

flyby_direction <- flyby_direction %>%
  mutate(
    direction_class = case_when(
      direction_final %in% c("from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide") ~ "from",
      direction_final %in% c("to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide")     ~ "to",
      direction_final == "return_flight"                          ~ "return",
      TRUE                                                        ~ "other"),
    direction_class = factor(direction_class, levels = c("from", "to", "return", "other")))

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
text:
Why this station is treated differently
Fullerton Entrance carries a single directional Yagi antenna (6-elements). Unlike the small omni-directional antennas used across the rest of the Motus array in the Hunter estuary (see Motus Array Maintenance), and capable of tracking site use directly, Fullerton Entrance station is located strategically: it sits on the corridor between the main area (estuary covered by several omni antennas) and the biggest and main mudflat of the area (Fullerton Cove), which has no antenna coverage at all because of its terrain configuration. So, in order to track movement and site use over this big mudflat (Fullerton Cove, or also called Fullerton mudflat), we placed a station right at the entry (Fullerton Entrance), to detect in-and-out passages.
Therefore, a tag detection at Fullerton Entrance station is either:

fly-by, the bird briefly fly by (in front of) the antenna, probably traveling between the estuary (roost?) and Fullerton mudflat (foraging?)
visits - the bird is actually sitting by the antenna itself, either roosting or foraging, using the site.

Since we cannot detect birds directly on Fullerton mudflat, we use fly-by detections at Fullerton Entrance station and their direction (another station → Fullerton Entrance or another station → Fullerton Entrance) as an indirect proxy for mudflat use.

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
text:
Set-up
As we will be re-using some of the data already loaded from previous workflow (see Station usage - hours (OBP method)), we will fetch here some of the objects we will re-use including: visit_duration, tide_data, data_all, recv, shorebird_class, and available_bird_recv_time.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(mixtools)
library(lubridate)
library(gt)

Now, we pre-fill some key-values we need to set-up the workflow.

focal_station    <- "Fullerton Entrance"   # the directional antenna

flyby_window_min <- 30                     # Period (min) before/after detection at Fullerton to look for a detection at another station

tide_lookahead_h <- 2                      # Period (hours) before/after of an "unknown" flyby detection used to infer direction from tide

# Keep only Fullerton Entrance data with visit duration (min)
fc_visits <- visit_duration %>%
  filter(recvDeployName == focal_station) %>%
  mutate(duration_min = duration_h * 60)

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
text:
Separate fly-by & site use
A very short visit (seconds to a couple of minutes) most likely reflects a bird flying by the antenna; while a longer visit likely reflects a bird actually using the site covered by antenna’s range coverage. We use the same mixture-model approach as for the detection-gap threshold (see Station usage - hours (OBP method)), but here fitted to visit durations at Fullerton Entrance only, to find a data-driven cut-off between “flyby” and “actual use”.
Fit a 2-component mixture model on log-transformed visit duration (component 1 = short/flyby, component 2 = long/actual use), and find the cut-point where the posterior probability of belonging to the “flyby” component drops below 0.5.

set.seed(123)

mix_fc <- normalmixEM(               # we assume normal distributions only
  log(fc_visits$duration_min + 1),   # +1 to avoid log(0), and log() used to compress/scale duration distributions and tails (i.e., lot of short vs few long)
  k = 2,                             # we assume two potential distribution (flyby and site use)
  maxit = 5000,                      # number of iteration to estimate what component each observation belogs to
  epsilon = 1e-08)                   # standard threshold value for estimation (convergence tolerance)

number of iterations= 21 

comp_order_fc <- order(mix_fc$mu)    # sort components -> comp_1 with smaller mean first (fly-by)

post_short    <- mix_fc$posterior[, comp_order_fc[1]] # extract first col of mix_fc$posterior, a matrix with one row per visit and one column per component, containing each visit's posterior probability of belonging to that component (rows sum to 1). So, post_short is a vector giving one value per visit of "probability this visit is a fly-by."

cut_df <- data.frame(duration_h = fc_visits$duration_h, p_short = post_short) %>%
  arrange(duration_h)

flyby_cutpoint_h <- cut_df$duration_h[which(cut_df$p_short < 0.5)[1]] # /!\ the value chosen here (0.5) finds the first duration in hour (smallest) where it has less than 50 % probability to be a fly-by /!\

Under 0.18 hours (~ 11 min), a detection at Fullerton Entrance is considered as a fly-by and above as a site use. So, let’s classify and visualise.

fc_visits <- fc_visits %>%
  mutate(visit_type = if_else(duration_h < flyby_cutpoint_h, "flyby", "actual_use"))

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
section: Infer the direction of each flyby
text:
Infer the direction of each flyby
For flyby events specifically, we want to know whether the bird was heading to the mudflat (last seen leaving the roost area, i.e. detected at another station shortly before the flyby) or coming from the mudflat (detected at another station shortly after the flyby). If both are true, the bird is treated as a return_flight seen at Fullerton Entrance on the way out and back; if neither, the direction is unknown and resolved separately using tide state (see below).

flyby_visits <- fc_visits %>% filter(visit_type == "flyby")

all_visits_dt   <- as.data.table(visit_duration)
other_visits_dt <- all_visits_dt[recvDeployName != focal_station]
flyby_dt        <- as.data.table(flyby_visits)

BEFORE match - closest other-station visit that ended within flyby_window_min minutes before the flyby started.

before_cand <- other_visits_dt[flyby_dt,
                               on = "Band.ID",
                               allow.cartesian = TRUE,
                               .(Band.ID, visitID = i.visitID,
                                 fc_start = i.visitStart,
                                 other_station = x.recvDeployName,
                                 other_end = x.visitEnd)]

before_cand <- before_cand[!is.na(other_end) &
                             other_end <= fc_start &
                             as.numeric(difftime(fc_start, other_end, units = "mins")) <= flyby_window_min]

# Keep only the closest (most recent) match per flyby event
before_flag <- before_cand[order(Band.ID, visitID, -as.numeric(other_end))][
  , .SD[1], by = .(Band.ID, visitID)][
  , .(Band.ID, visitID, before_station = other_station, before_end = other_end)]

AFTER match - closest other-station visit that started within flyby_window_min minutes after the flyby ended (mirror image of the BEFORE match above).

after_cand <- other_visits_dt[flyby_dt,
                              on = "Band.ID",
                              allow.cartesian = TRUE,
                              .(Band.ID, visitID = i.visitID,
                                fc_end = i.visitEnd,
                                other_station = x.recvDeployName,
                                other_start = x.visitStart)]

after_cand <- after_cand[!is.na(other_start) &
                           other_start >= fc_end &
                           as.numeric(difftime(other_start, fc_end, units = "mins")) <= flyby_window_min]

# Keep only the closest (earliest) match per flyby event
after_flag <- after_cand[order(Band.ID, visitID, as.numeric(other_start))][
  , .SD[1], by = .(Band.ID, visitID)][
  , .(Band.ID, visitID, after_station = other_station, after_start = other_start)]

Classify direction from the presence/absence of a BEFORE and/or AFTER match.

flyby_direction <- flyby_visits %>%
  left_join(as.data.frame(before_flag), by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  left_join(as.data.frame(after_flag),  by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(
    has_before = !is.na(before_end),
    has_after  = !is.na(after_start),
    direction = case_when(
      has_before & has_after  ~ "return_flight",
      has_before & !has_after ~ "to_mudflat",
      !has_before & has_after ~ "from_mudflat",
      TRUE                    ~ "unknown"))


Resolving the “unknown” flybys with tide state
For flybys with no other-station match on either side, direction cannot be resolved from detections alone. As a fallback, we look at the tide state around the flyby: if the tide is rising toward High in the following hours, the bird is more likely heading from the mudflat (leaving as it floods); if it is falling toward Low, the bird is more likely heading to the mudflat (arriving as it drains).

tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[, .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]
setkey(tide_dt, tideDateTimeAus)

infer_tide_direction <- function(start_time, lookahead_h = tide_lookahead_h) {
  hrs    <- seq(from = start_time, by = "hour", length.out = lookahead_h + 1)
  hrs_dt <- data.table(hour_dt = hrs)
  matched <- tide_dt[hrs_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
  n_high <- sum(grepl("High", matched$tideCategory))
  n_low  <- sum(grepl("Low",  matched$tideCategory))
  if (n_high > n_low) return("from_mudflat_tide")
  if (n_low > n_high) return("to_mudflat_tide")
  "ambiguous_tide"
}

unknown_flyby <- flyby_direction %>%
  filter(direction == "unknown") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(inferred_direction = infer_tide_direction(visitStart)) %>%
  ungroup()

flyby_direction <- flyby_direction %>%
  left_join(unknown_flyby %>% select(Band.ID, visitID, inferred_direction),
            by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(direction_final = if_else(direction == "unknown" & !is.na(inferred_direction),
                                    inferred_direction, direction))










We simplify direction_final into a broader direction_class (from / to / return / other) for plotting.

flyby_direction <- flyby_direction %>%
  mutate(
    direction_class = case_when(
      direction_final %in% c("from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide") ~ "from",
      direction_final %in% c("to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide")     ~ "to",
      direction_final == "return_flight"                          ~ "return",
      TRUE                                                        ~ "other"),
    direction_class = factor(direction_class, levels = c("from", "to", "return", "other")))

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
section: Step 3 - Combine flyby and site-use classifications
text:
Step 3 - Combine flyby and site-use classifications
We now bring visit_type (flyby / actual_use) and direction_final back together into a single table covering all Fullerton Entrance visits, so that “site use” sits alongside the flyby directions as one classification.

    by = c("Band.ID", "visitID")) %>%
  mutate(direction_final = if_else(visit_type == "actual_use", "site_use", direction_final))

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
section: Step 4 - Estimate hours spent at the mudflat vs at Fullerton Entrance
text:
Step 4 - Estimate hours spent at the mudflat vs at Fullerton Entrance
For site_use events, the duration a bird spent at Fullerton Entrance is simply duration_h of the visit itself. For to_mudflat/from_mudflat flybys there is no direct duration - instead we use the surrounding tide turning point as a proxy boundary for how long the bird likely remained on the mudflat:

to_mudflat - from the moment the bird was last seen (visitEnd) forward to the next tide turning point (i.e. the remainder of the current tide phase).
from_mudflat - from the previous tide turning point back to the moment the bird was detected (visitStart) (i.e. how long the current tide phase had already run before the bird arrived).


# Nearest tide turning point before / after a given timestamp
tide_times <- sort(tide_data$tideDateTimeAus)

next_tide_turn <- function(t) {
  cand <- tide_times[tide_times > t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  min(cand)
}
prev_tide_turn <- function(t) {
  cand <- tide_times[tide_times < t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  max(cand)
}

# Dominant tideCategory across a time window (hourly expansion, nearest-tide join)
tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[order(tideDateTimeAus), .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]

dominant_tide <- function(w_start, w_end) {
  if (is.na(w_start) || is.na(w_end) || w_end <= w_start) return(NA_character_)
  hrs    <- seq(floor_date(w_start, "hour"), floor_date(w_end, "hour"), by = "hour")
  hrs_dt <- data.table(hour_dt = hrs)
  matched <- tide_dt[hrs_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
  names(sort(table(matched$tideCategory), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
}

Build the per-visit duration/tide table, keeping only site_use and mudflat-direction events (return flights and unresolved flybys are excluded, since we cannot bound a mudflat window for them).

plot_data <- fc_classified %>%
  filter(direction_final %in% c("site_use", "to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide",
                                "from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    category = if_else(direction_final == "site_use",
                       "Fullerton entrance", "Fullerton mudflat"),
    win_start = case_when(
      direction_final == "site_use" ~ visitStart,
      direction_final %in% c("to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide")   ~ visitEnd,
      direction_final %in% c("from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide") ~ prev_tide_turn(visitStart)),
    win_end = case_when(
      direction_final == "site_use" ~ visitEnd,
      direction_final %in% c("to_mudflat", "to_mudflat_tide")   ~ next_tide_turn(visitEnd),
      direction_final %in% c("from_mudflat", "from_mudflat_tide") ~ visitStart),
    duration_h_final = as.numeric(difftime(win_end, win_start, units = "hours")),
    tideCategory_dom  = dominant_tide(win_start, win_end),
    tideDiel = if_else(grepl("Diurnal", tideCategory_dom), "Diurnal", "Nocturnal")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(duration_h_final), duration_h_final > 0)


Rate of use, referenced to Fullerton Entrance availability
Because “Fullerton mudflat” is an inferred location rather than a real receiver, both categories are expressed as a rate against the same denominator: the hours Fullerton Entrance was available (station on + bird tagged and alive), per bird and per diel period. This comes from available_bird_recv_time, computed in the previous chapter.

# Available hours at Fullerton Entrance, per bird / species / diel period
available_fc <- available_bird_recv_time %>%
  filter(recvDeployName == "Fullerton Entrance") %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, tideDiel) %>%
  summarise(available_h = sum(duration_h), .groups = "drop")

# Used hours per bird / category / diel period, then compute rate of use (%)
plot_summary <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, category, tideDiel) %>%
  summarise(used_h = sum(duration_h_final), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(available_fc, by = c("Band.ID", "speciesEN", "tideDiel")) %>%
  mutate(rate_use = (used_h / available_h) * 100,
         rate_use = pmin(rate_use, 100))  # cap: a few cases exceed 100% (see note below)


Note: a small number of birds show rate_use above 100%, since mudflat duration is inferred from tide turning points rather than directly observed, and can occasionally exceed the bird’s directly-available Fullerton Entrance time. These values are capped at 100% rather than excluded.

Set-up data
As we will be re-using some of the data already loaded from previous workflow (see Station usage - hours (OBP method)), we will fetch here some of the objects we will re-use including: visit_duration, tide_data, data_all, recv, shorebird_class, and available_bird_recv_time.

visit_duration is then used onward so, the same rule applies in the data-set: < 1 hour gap between two runs are considered as a unique use of the area covered by a Motus station - the bird remained in the area within this hour gap.


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(mixtools)
library(lubridate)
library(gt)
library(lubridate)
library(ggpattern)

Now, we pre-fill some key-values we need to set-up the workflow.

focal_station    <- "Fullerton Entrance"   # the directional antenna

flyby_window_min <- 30                     # Period (min) before/after detection at Fullerton to look for a detection at another station

tide_lookahead_h <- 2                      # Period (hours) before/after of an "unknown" flyby detection used to infer direction from tide

# Keep only Fullerton Entrance data with visit duration (min)
fc_passages <- visit_duration %>%
  filter(recvDeployName == focal_station) %>%
  mutate(duration_min = duration_h * 60)


CountDuration

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
text:
When is it a fly-by?

Note: Onward, a detection will be called a passage, an long passage reflecting an actual use of the site will be called a visit and a short passage reflecting a fly-by will be called a fly-by.

A very short passage (seconds to a couple of minutes) most likely reflects a bird flying by the antenna; while a longer passage likely reflects a bird actually using the site covered by antenna’s range coverage. We use the same mixture-model approach as for the detection-gap threshold (see Station usage - hours (OBP method)), but here fitted to passage durations at Fullerton Entrance only, to find a data-driven cut-off between “flyby” and “visit”.
Fit a 2-component mixture model on log-transformed passage duration (component 1 = short/flyby, component 2 = long/actual use), and find the cut-point where the posterior probability of belonging to the “fly-by” component drops below 0.5.

set.seed(123)

mix_fc <- normalmixEM(               # we assume normal distributions only
  log(fc_passages$duration_min + 1),   # +1 to avoid log(0), and log() used to compress/scale duration distributions and tails (i.e., lot of short vs few long)
  k = 2,                             # we assume two potential distribution (flyby and visits)
  maxit = 5000,                      # number of iteration to estimate what component each observation belongs to
  epsilon = 1e-08)                   # standard threshold value for estimation (convergence tolerance)

number of iterations= 21 

comp_order_fc <- order(mix_fc$mu)    # sort components -> comp_1 with smaller mean first (fly-by)

post_short    <- mix_fc$posterior[, comp_order_fc[1]] # extract first col of mix_fc$posterior, a matrix with one row per passage and one column per component, containing each passage's posterior probability of belonging to that component (rows sum to 1). So, post_short is a vector giving one value per passage of "probability this passage is a fly-by."

cut_df <- data.frame(duration_h = fc_passages$duration_h, p_short = post_short) %>%
  arrange(duration_h)

flyby_cutpoint_h <- cut_df$duration_h[which(cut_df$p_short < 0.5)[1]] # /!\ the value chosen here (0.5) finds the first duration in hour (smallest) where it has less than 50 % probability to be a fly-by /!\

Under 0.18 hours (~ 11 min), a detection at Fullerton Entrance is considered as a fly-by and above as a visit. So, let’s classify and visualise.

fc_passages <- fc_passages %>%
  mutate(passage_type = if_else(duration_h < flyby_cutpoint_h, "flyby", "visit"))

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
text:
Fly-by direction
For flyby events specifically, we want to know whether the bird was heading to the mudflat (last seen leaving the roost area, i.e. detected at another station shortly before the flyby) or coming from the mudflat (detected at another station shortly after the flyby). To do so, we need to understand what is the right temporal window to consider for defining the “shortly after” or “shortly before”, and to rely on inference only when the detection into another Motus station is beyond this value.
Let’s start by splitting the data-set accordingly before to estimate the direction of a fly-by depending on the tide: toward the mudflat of Fullerton cove if the fly-by is detected during a dropping tide, and inversely if detected during a rising tide.

flyby_passages <- fc_passages %>% filter(passage_type == "flyby")

all_passages_dt   <- as.data.table(visit_duration)
other_passages_dt <- all_passages_dt[recvDeployName != focal_station]
flyby_dt        <- as.data.table(flyby_passages)


flyby_dt <- flyby_dt %>%
  
  rowwise() %>%
  
  mutate(
    closest_tide = list(
      tide_data %>%
        mutate(diff_time = abs(as.numeric(difftime(tideDateTimeAus, visitStart, units = "mins")))) %>%
        slice_min(diff_time, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)),  # single closest tide, either side of visitStart
    
    nearestTideDiel   = closest_tide$day_night[1],
    nearestTideLevel  = closest_tide$high_low[1],
    nearestTideTime   = closest_tide$tideDateTimeAus[1]) %>%
  
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-closest_tide) %>%
  
  mutate(
    direction = case_when(
      nearestTideLevel == "High" ~ "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)",
      nearestTideLevel == "Low"  ~ "TO mudflat (dropping tide)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_ ))


barplot(table(flyby_dt$direction, useNA = "ifany"),
        main = "Inferred flyby direction based on next tide",
        ylab = "Count of flybys")








For each fly-by detected at Fullerton Entrance, we then look for a confirming detection at another Motus station: if the tide was rising, we check for the closest following detection after Fullerton Entrance; if the tide was dropping, we check for the closest preceding detection before Fullerton Entrance.

flyby_dt <- flyby_dt %>%
  
  rowwise() %>%
  
  mutate(
    .band    = as.character(Band.ID),
    .start   = visitStart,
    .station = recvDeployName,
    
    other_passage = list(
      if (direction == "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)") {
        all_passages_dt %>%
          filter(as.character(Band.ID) == .band,
                 recvDeployName != .station,
                 visitStart >= .start) %>%
          slice_min(visitStart, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else if (direction == "TO mudflat (dropping tide)") {
        all_passages_dt %>%
          filter(as.character(Band.ID) == .band,
                 recvDeployName != .station,
                 visitStart <= .start) %>%
          slice_max(visitStart, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else {
        all_passages_dt %>% filter(FALSE)
      }
    ),
    
    side_detection = other_passage$recvDeployName[1],
    side_time      = other_passage$visitStart[1],
    delay_min      = as.numeric(abs(difftime(.start, other_passage$visitStart[1], units = "mins")))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-other_passage, -.band, -.start, -.station)

We then look at the distribution of the delay between a Fly-By detection at Fullerton entrance and another Motus station, in order to identify a temporal window we can use as a cut-off for concluding that “the bird flew continuously between the fly-by detection at Fullerton Entrance and the next detection at another Motus station” (or, in the reverse case, between a detection at another station and the fly-by at Fullerton entrance during a dropping tide).
We first filter out any extreme tail in the data, then visualise the distribution to estimate how many underlying components it contains.




















So we visually decided to filter out delays of more than 4000 min (~ 2.8 days).

flyby_dt_trimmed  <- flyby_dt %>% 
  filter(delay_min < 4000)


flyby_dt_trimmed %>%
  pull(delay_min) %>%
  hist(breaks = 100,
       main  = "Delay to (or period before) nearest next site detection",
       xlab  = "Delay (minutes)") 







flyby_dt_trimmed %>%
  filter(delay_min < 100) %>%
  pull(delay_min) %>%
  hist(breaks = 100,
       main  = "Delay to (or period before) nearest next site detection",
       xlab  = "Delay (minutes)") 








Visually, we can estimate that the overall temporal window for “continuous flights” between the Fullerton entrance and another Motus station is about 10 minutes. However, we can fit an N-mixture model to confirm this.

delay_vals <- na.omit(flyby_dt_trimmed$delay_min)
set.seed(1)  # EM is stochastic in its starting values
mix <- normalmixEM(delay_vals, 
                   k = 2)
plot(mix, which = 2)







# order components so mu1 < mu2 (short-delay vs long-delay cluster)
ord    <- order(mix$mu)
mu     <- mix$mu[ord]
sigma  <- mix$sigma[ord]
lambda <- mix$lambda[ord]

# find where the two weighted densities cross, between the two means
f <- function(x) lambda[1]*dnorm(x, mu[1], sigma[1]) - lambda[2]*dnorm(x, mu[2], sigma[2])
flyby_window_min <- uniroot(f, lower = mu[1], upper = mu[2])$root
flyby_window_min

With a statistically determined threshold, any delay between a detection at the Fullerton entrance and a another Motus station that is shorter than 10.8395932 minutes will be treated as a verified flight direction for the bird. Beyond this value, a continuous flight inferred from a double-detection data based might not be considered realistic, suggesting detection at another Motus station cannot be trusted to infer the bird’s flight direction.
See below for the distribution of these results.

flyby_dt <- flyby_dt %>%
  mutate(retained_cut = case_when(
    # is.na(delay)                    ~ "inferred_only",
    delay_min <= flyby_window_min   ~ "Verified by another Motus station detection",
    TRUE                            ~ "Inferred only from tide data"))


bp_data <- t(table(flyby_dt$direction, flyby_dt$retained_cut))

bp <- barplot(bp_data,
              beside = TRUE,
              legend.text = FALSE,
              main = paste0("Direction by confirmation \nwith another detection before ",
                             round(flyby_window_min, 1), " min (cutpoint)"),
              ylab = "Count of flybys")

legend("bottom",
       inset = c(0, -0.37),
       legend = rownames(bp_data),
       fill = gray.colors(nrow(bp_data)),
       xpd = TRUE,
       bty = "n")

  filter(retained_cut == "Verified by another Motus station detection") %>%

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
text:
Fullerton cove & Fullerton entrance
For site_use events, the duration a bird spent at Fullerton Entrance is simply duration_h of the visit itself. For to_mudflat/from_mudflat flybys there is no direct duration - instead we use the surrounding tide turning point as a proxy boundary for how long the bird likely remained on the mudflat:

to_mudflat - from the moment the bird was last seen (visitEnd) forward to the next tide turning point (i.e. the remainder of the current tide phase).
from_mudflat - from the previous tide turning point back to the moment the bird was detected (visitStart) (i.e. how long the current tide phase had already run before the bird arrived).


# Nearest tide turning point before / after a given timestamp
tide_times <- sort(tide_data$tideDateTimeAus)

next_tide_turn <- function(t) {
  cand <- tide_times[tide_times > t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  min(cand)
}
prev_tide_turn <- function(t) {
  cand <- tide_times[tide_times < t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  max(cand)
}

# Dominant tideCategory across a time window (hourly expansion, nearest-tide join)
tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[order(tideDateTimeAus), .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]

dominant_tide <- function(w_start, w_end) {
  if (is.na(w_start) || is.na(w_end) || w_end <= w_start) return(NA_character_)
  hrs    <- seq(floor_date(w_start, "hour"), floor_date(w_end, "hour"), by = "hour")
  hrs_dt <- data.table(hour_dt = hrs)
  matched <- tide_dt[hrs_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
  names(sort(table(matched$tideCategory), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
}

Build the per-visit duration/tide table, keeping only site_use and mudflat-direction events (return flights and unresolved flybys are excluded, since we cannot bound a mudflat window for them).

plot_data <- fc_classified %>% 
  mutate(direction = replace_na(direction, "Actual site use")) %>% ## Be careful and know your data here
  
  filter(direction %in% c("Actual site use", 
                          "To mudflat (falling tide)",
                          "From mudflat (rising tide)")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    category = if_else(direction == "Actual site use",
                       "Fullerton entrance", "Fullerton mudflat"),
    win_start = case_when(
      direction == "Actual site use"                    ~ visitStart,
      direction == "To mudflat (falling tide)"    ~ visitEnd,
      direction == "From mudflat (rising tide)"   ~ prev_tide_turn(visitStart)),
    win_end = case_when(
      direction == "Actual site use"                    ~ visitEnd,
      direction == "To mudflat (falling tide)"    ~ next_tide_turn(visitEnd),
      direction == "From mudflat (rising tide)"   ~ visitStart),
    duration_h_final = as.numeric(difftime(win_end, win_start, units = "hours")),
    tideCategory_dom  = dominant_tide(win_start, win_end),
    tideDiel = if_else(grepl("Diurnal", tideCategory_dom), "Diurnal", "Nocturnal")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(duration_h_final), duration_h_final > 0)

title: Site use - hours (Fullerton case)
text:
Rate of use
For visits, the duration a bird spent at Fullerton Entrance is simply duration_h of the visit itself.
For fly-bys there is no direct duration: instead, we estimate how long the bird likely remained on the mudflat using either a corroborating detection at another Motus station, or, when none is available, the surrounding tide turning point as a proxy boundary:
TO mudflat (dropping tide) — if the bird was subsequently detected at another station near the next tide event, the duration runs from the moment it was detected here (visitEnd) to that corroborating detection (double_detection). Otherwise, the duration runs from visitEnd to the next tide turning point.
BACK from mudflat (rising tide) — if the bird was previously detected as a flyby near the last tide event, the duration runs from that corroborating detection to the moment it was detected here (visitStart) (double_detection). Otherwise, the duration runs from the previous tide turning point to visitStart.
Let’s first estimate/compute the time spent into Fullerton mudflat for the fly-bys.

# Turning points: midpoint between each consecutive pair of tide extremes
tide_times     <- sort(unique(tide_data$tideDateTimeAus))
turning_points <- tide_times[-length(tide_times)] + diff(tide_times) / 2

next_turning_point <- function(t) {
  cand <- turning_points[turning_points > t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  min(cand)
}
prev_turning_point <- function(t) {
  cand <- turning_points[turning_points < t]
  if (length(cand) == 0) return(as.POSIXct(NA))
  max(cand)
}

flyby_dt <- flyby_dt %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    .band      = as.character(Band.ID),
    .start     = visitStart,
    .station   = recvDeployName,
    .tide_time = nearestTideTime,
    
    # Find the closest detection at another station, searched in the
    # correct direction relative to nearestTideTime
    match_visit = list(
      if (direction == "TO mudflat (dropping tide)") {
        # nearestTideTime is AFTER visitStart -> search forward
        all_passages_dt %>%
          filter(as.character(Band.ID) == .band,
                 recvDeployName != .station,
                 visitStart > .start) %>%
          mutate(diff_to_tide = abs(as.numeric(difftime(visitStart, .tide_time, units = "mins")))) %>%
          slice_min(diff_to_tide, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else if (direction == "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)") {
        # nearestTideTime is BEFORE visitStart -> search backward
        all_passages_dt %>%
          filter(as.character(Band.ID) == .band,
                 recvDeployName != .station,
                 visitStart < .start) %>%
          mutate(diff_to_tide = abs(as.numeric(difftime(visitStart, .tide_time, units = "mins")))) %>%
          slice_min(diff_to_tide, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
      } else {
        all_passages_dt %>% filter(FALSE)
      } ),
    
    side_detection = match_visit$recvDeployName[1],
    side_time      = match_visit$visitStart[1],
    
    time_used_type = case_when(
      passage_type != "flyby" ~ NA_character_,
      !is.na(side_time)     ~ "double_detection",
      TRUE                  ~ "single_detection"),
    
    turning_point = case_when(
      direction == "TO mudflat (dropping tide)" ~ next_turning_point(.start),
      direction == "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)" ~ prev_turning_point(.start),
      TRUE ~ as.POSIXct(NA) ),
    
    time_used = case_when(
      passage_type != "flyby"                ~ as.numeric(NA),
      time_used_type == "double_detection" ~ as.numeric(abs(difftime(side_time, .start, units = "hours"))),
      time_used_type == "single_detection" ~ as.numeric(abs(difftime(turning_point, .start, units = "hours"))),
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)) ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-match_visit, -.band, -.start, -.station, -.tide_time)

Let’s now add the duration between visits to a Motus station area and the inferred time spent into the mudflat from fly-bys.

# Dominant tideCategory across a time window (hourly expansion, nearest-tide join)
tide_dt <- as.data.table(tide_data)[order(tideDateTimeAus), .(tideDateTimeAus, tideCategory)]

dominant_tide <- function(w_start, w_end) {
  if (is.na(w_start) || is.na(w_end) || w_end <= w_start) return(NA_character_)
  hrs    <- seq(floor_date(w_start, "hour"), floor_date(w_end, "hour"), by = "hour")
  hrs_dt <- data.table(hour_dt = hrs)
  matched <- tide_dt[hrs_dt, on = .(tideDateTimeAus = hour_dt), roll = "nearest"]
  names(sort(table(matched$tideCategory), decreasing = TRUE))[1]}

# get actual site-use rows from fc_classified
fc_classified_clean <- fc_classified %>%
  filter(passage_type == "visit") %>%
  mutate(time_used = duration_h) ## in  hour!!!

# combine with flyby_dt
plot_data <- bind_rows(flyby_dt,  fc_classified_clean)

plot_data <- plot_data %>%    
  mutate(direction = replace_na(direction, "Visits")) %>%
  
  filter(direction %in% c("Visits", 
                           "TO mudflat (dropping tide)",
                           "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    category = if_else(direction == "Visits",
                        "Fullerton entrance (Motus station)", "Fullerton cove (mudflat)"),
    
    win_start = case_when(
      direction == "Visits" ~ visitStart,
      direction == "TO mudflat (dropping tide)" ~ visitEnd,
      direction == "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)" & time_used_type == "double_detection" ~ side_time,
      direction == "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)" ~ turning_point),
    win_end = case_when(
      direction == "Visits" ~ visitEnd,
      direction == "TO mudflat (dropping tide)" & time_used_type == "double_detection" ~ side_time,
      direction == "TO mudflat (dropping tide)" ~ turning_point,
      direction == "BACK from mudflat (rising tide)" ~ visitStart),
    
    tideCategory = dominant_tide(win_start, win_end),
    tideDiel     = if_else(grepl("Diurnal", tideCategory), "Diurnal", "Nocturnal")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(time_used), time_used > 0)

Because “Fullerton mudflat” is an inferred location rather than an actual listening Motus station, both categories are expressed as a rate against the same denominator: the hours Fullerton Entrance Motus station was available (station ON + bird tagged and alive), per bird and per diel period. This comes from available_bird_recv_time, computed in the previous chapter.

# Available hours at Fullerton Entrance, per bird / species / diel period
available_fc <- available_bird_recv_time %>%
  filter(recvDeployName == "Fullerton Entrance") %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, tideDiel) %>%
  summarise(available_h = sum(duration_h), .groups = "drop")

# Used hours per bird / category / diel period, then compute rate of use (%)
plot_summary <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(Band.ID, speciesEN, category, tideDiel) %>%
  summarise(used_h = sum(time_used), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(available_fc, by = c("Band.ID", "speciesEN", "tideDiel")) %>%
  mutate(rate_use = (used_h / available_h) * 100,
         rate_use = pmin(rate_use, 100))  # cap: a few cases exceed 100% (see note below)


Note: a small number of birds show rate_use above 100%, since mudflat duration is inferred from tide turning points rather than directly observed, and can occasionally exceed the bird’s directly-available Fullerton Entrance time. These values are capped at 100% rather than excluded.
